senses.gloss: (b. h.; cmp. כאב)to grow dim, to be extinguished, go out.
units: <cite ref="Shabbat 21a:12">Sabb. 21ᵃ</cite> <he>כָּבְתָה זקוק לה</he> if the Ḥănuckah light went out, he is bound to attend to it.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 2:2:3">Y. Yoma II, 39ᵈ</cite> <he>קטורת שכָּבַת</he> frankincense which went out (was not entirely burnt).
<cite ref="Shabbat 30b:2">Sabb. 30ᵇ</cite> <he>מוטב תִּכְבֶּה נרו וכ׳</he> it is better that a human light (candle) be extinguished, than that God’s light (life) be extinguished; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to extinguish. Ib.ᵃ לא יְכַבֶּה ואם כִּבָּה פטור he must not put it out, but if he did &c. Ib. II, 5 המְכַבֶּה את הנר he who puts the (Sabbath) lamp out.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 68:10">Gen. R. s. 68</cite> (play on <he>כי בא</he>, <cite ref="Genesis 28:11">Gen. XXVIII, 11</cite>) <he>כִּיבָּא השמש</he> (some ed. <cite ref="K00047"><he>כיבה</he></cite>) He extinguished the sun (made the sun set earlier).

<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 13:9">Tosef. Sabb. XIII</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 14:9">XIV</cite>), 9 <he>נכרי שבא לכַבּוֹת אין אומ׳ לו כַּבֵּה ואל תְּכַבֶּה</he> if a gentile comes (on the Sabbath) to extinguish (a fire), we say to him neither ‘extinguish’ nor ‘do not’. Gen. R. l. c. <he>אמר המלך כַּבּוּ וכ׳</he> (not <he>כיבו</he>) said the king, put out &c.; a. fr.
